headline: Regional Coastal Access and Seasonal Peak Lodging
reservation: While Twillingate has no entry gates or day-use permits, high-season lodging and boat tours are significant bottlenecks. Visitors should verify availability months in advance as coastal capacities are fixed, and check local maritime operators for changing schedule requirements during iceberg and whale seasons.

days.title: Iceberg Alley and Coastal Vistas

stops.name: Long Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: Constructed in 1876, this high-altitude beacon offers expansive views of the Atlantic and is a prime spot for spotting migrating icebergs in early summer.

stops.name: Lower Little Harbour Trail
stops.detail: Walk the coastal path to see the natural arch formations and rugged cliffs that define this stretch of the Kittiwake Coast.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transitions; conditions vary by weather
days.note: Fog can roll in rapidly, obscuring visibility at the lighthouse.

days.title: Islands and Outport Heritage

stops.name: Durrell Museum
stops.detail: Explore the region's fishing history and view the massive stuffed polar bear exhibit, reflecting the area's subarctic influences.

stops.name: Prime Berth Fishing Museum
stops.detail: Learn about the traditional cod fishery and see whale skeletons at this privately operated heritage site near the causeway.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for short hops between islands; conditions vary
days.note: Local museums have seasonal hours; confirm locally upon arrival.

days.title: Wilderness Coves and Sea Kayaking

stops.name: Spiller's Cove
stops.detail: Observe the dramatic sea stacks and look for nesting seabirds along the jagged shoreline.

stops.name: Nanny's Hole
stops.detail: A sheltered cove ideal for observing the intersection of the rocky terrain and the North Atlantic swells.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local gravel roads; conditions vary
days.note: Sea conditions dictate water access; always check marine forecasts.

intel.title: Lighthouse Congestion
intel.text: The Long Point Lighthouse parking area is small and often reaches capacity during peak iceberg months. Additional space is sometimes available at trailheads, but visitors should have a secondary plan during midday.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is generally reliable in the main townsite but drops off significantly on the outer coastal trails and Spiller's Cove. Download offline maps for navigation through the island network.

intel.title: Supply Nodes
intel.text: Twillingate serves as the primary hub for fuel and groceries for the surrounding islands. It is prudent to top up before exploring the more remote reaches of the Kittiwake Coast.

intel.title: Seasonality of Ice
intel.text: Iceberg sightings typically peak in May and June, while whale sightings are more common in July and August. Adjust your visit dates based on which natural phenomenon you prioritize.

intel.title: Causeway Transit
intel.text: The islands are connected to the mainland via the Road to the Isles (Route 340) causeways. High winds can occasionally impact high-profile vehicle stability during crossing.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Gander International (YQX) and secure supplies in Gander before the two-hour drive north to the Twillingate islands.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; check rental agreements for gravel road restrictions on coastal access routes.
plan.goldenHour: Long Point Lighthouse for sunset, with clarity dependent on the presence of coastal fog banks.
